rows.evasion: Split the demand: ₹9,500 four times to one payee during the call
rows.observed: each of the 4 payments was paused, paused, paused, paused; the trigger counts what was already sent during the call and the payee stays new for the rest of the call
rows.why: v0.3: amounts sent during the call add up; a payee first paid during the call stays new.

rows.evasion: Hang up, wait 30 minutes, then pay ₹60,000
rows.observed: assessed: call ended 30.0 min ago, new payee, amount >= 10,000

rows.evasion: Hang up, wait 30 minutes, then pay ₹40,000
rows.observed: not assessed: the call ended 30 min ago, outside the window for this amount (payment rules met: new payee, amount >= 10,000)
rows.why: Open gap. Next: a per-user window, or the bank's velocity rules on new payees.

rows.evasion: Coach the victim to answer "No one asked me"
rows.observed: tier green after the coached answer; the cue checklist comes first (cue_secrecy, cue_otp_pin, cue_arrest_threat). Coached to tap "None of these" as well: tier green, the payment can go
rows.why: The three questions come first, and the UI says being told what to tap is a warning sign. A victim coached through every question still gets through: the residual risk.

rows.evasion: Coach the victim to say "a shop or UPI app"
rows.observed: tier green after the coached answer; the cue checklist comes first (cue_otp_pin, cue_remote_app, cue_refund_verification). Coached to tap "None of these" as well: tier green, the payment can go
rows.why: v0.3: the checklist now covers this claim too, with the refund-script questions. A victim coached through every question still gets through: the residual risk.

rows.evasion: Call from a spoofed 1600 bank number
rows.observed: registry: no_active_call; tier red, status held
rows.why: The bank's own call registry says it isn't calling: a decisive negative from outside the call.

rows.evasion: Caller ID shows the son's saved number (spoofed, or his WhatsApp taken over)
rows.observed: tier green after "Family member", and Family Verify still went to the son's own phone; he answered no: tier red, status held
rows.why: v0.3: Family Verify goes out even at Green. The son's own phone is the check the attacker can't fake.

rows.evasion: Mule account opened in the son's name
rows.observed: tier green after "Family member", and Family Verify still went to the son's own phone; he answered no: tier red, status held
rows.why: v0.3: no name mismatch to see, so the son's own answer decides, even at Green.

rows.evasion: Swap in the attacker's phone as the son's, mid-attack
rows.observed: re-binding refused (409); the attacker's 'yes' rejected (403); the son's real answer accepted (200)
rows.why: v0.3: no re-binding while a question waits. Production: bank-app device binding (not built).

rows.observed: a 'yes' signed for an earlier question: 403; tampered nonce: 403
rows.why: Each answer is signed over the challenge id and a fresh nonce by the son's device key.

rows.evasion: Spam Family Verify until the son taps yes or tunes out
rows.observed: push requests 2-4 returned [200, 200, 429]; then: "Too many Family Verify requests in the last hour. Call Rahul on their saved number instead."
rows.why: v0.3: 3 pushes per payer and 5 per relative per hour, then "call him on his saved number".

rows.evasion: A clone the detector misses (cloned son, son says no)
rows.observed: voice band no_strong_evidence (shadow); tier before red, after red; user message: "Thanks — this is saved with your case. Voice checks can't yet confirm who is calling on a phone line, so please use the checks above."
rows.why: G2: voice is shadow-only, so a missed clone can't release money.

rows.evasion: Detector false alarm on the real son (son says yes)
rows.observed: voice band likely_synthetic (shadow); tier before green, after green; user message: "Thanks — this is saved with your case. Voice checks can't yet confirm who is calling on a phone line, so please use the checks above."
rows.why: G2 and G6: voice can't hold money and the copy never accuses the caller.

rows.evasion: WhatsApp or VoIP call instead of a phone call
rows.observed: trigger: call active, new payee, amount >= 10,000; signals ['caller_unknown', 'caller_voip_unknown', 'payee_new']
rows.why: The Android audio mode shows an ongoing VoIP call; unknown VoIP callers add risk.

rows.evasion: Many small payments to new payees, no call
rows.observed: no call, three new payees at ₹4,000: burst signal per payment [False, False, False], assessed [False, False, False]. With no call Pehchaan stays out by design (SPEC section 2); the burst signal counts once a call is on
rows.why: By design (SPEC section 2): no call, no Pehchaan. The bank's own fraud rules still apply.

rows.evasion: Many small payments to new payees during a call
rows.observed: on a call, three new payees at ₹4,000: each paused; burst signal [False, True, True]
rows.why: burst_new_payees now counts real payments in the last 30 minutes.

declared.evasion: Pay from another UPI app that doesn't have Pehchaan
declared.status: Not covered by the app SDK. At a bank deployment the risk API sees every debit from the account, but without the call state, so only payee and amount context.

declared.evasion: Screen-share or remote-control app (the scammer taps for the victim)
declared.status: Not detected today. Android can tell an app that screen sharing or an accessibility service is active: we would add that as a context signal.

declared.evasion: The scammer coaches the real son, or the son is in on it
declared.status: Family Verify trusts the bound relative. The son sees the payee name and amount; the case stays in the analyst queue; large amounts need an analyst to release a hold.

declared.evasion: The scammer adds their own phone to the family circle before the attack
declared.status: Both sides opt in. Production binding goes through the bank app's authenticated device binding with a waiting period for new relatives; the prototype binds the relative page when it opens.

note: Fresh demo per row, fictional people, mock context adapters and mock voice service.
